items.text: Bahrain's military says that they have intercepted a number of missiles and drones from Iran. ((Arab News))
Jordan's military says that they have intercepted seven missiles and six drones launched from Iran. No casualties or damage were reported. ((Al-Monitor))
Kuwait's army says that its air defenses confronted several attacks from Iran. ((Arab News))
Iran says it has attacked U.S. military bases in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait, including the Isa Air Base, using Arash drones. ((Euronews))

The U.S. military says its forces fired into a tanker's engine room and disabled the vessel after its crew repeatedly attempted to breach the American blockade of Iranian ports and ignored warnings. ((AFP via BSS))

The Indian embassy in Tehran reports that the Mozambique-flagged LPG tanker Disha with 28 Indian nationals on the vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. All 28 crew members were reported safe. ((The Hindustan Times)) ((India Today))
The United States strikes an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy headquarters in Ziba Kenar, Gilan province, Iran. ((Arab News)) ((Iran International))
Drones target Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan Region, with six drones reported to be intercepted. ((AP)) ((Kurdistan24))

The Wall Street Journal reports that Bahraini and Kuwaiti fighter jets attacked military targets inside Iran earlier in July, with air and intelligence support from the United Arab Emirates. ((The Wall Street Journal)) ((The Jerusalem Post))

The Israeli military reports that the air force has struck Hamas weapon depots, weapon manufacturing sites and tunnels in the Gaza Strip, and accuses the militant group of violating the ceasefire signed in October 2025. ((The Times of Israel))

Clashes in Tell, Nablus, kill four Palestinians and two Israelis after a confrontation between settlers and locals in the town. Subsequent settler attacks in the West Bank injure at least 10 Palestinians. ((Haaretz)) ((The New York Times))

The Houthis deny reports that they have closed the Bab-el-Mandeb and state that they are not seeking to close it, reaffirming that they have only established a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia. ((DW)) ((Middle East Eye))
Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi military sites in Hodeidah, Yemen, after a long hiatus in response to the movement's attacks on maritime shipping, while the militant group vows to retaliate. ((Reuters))
A Wildberries logistic hub in Russia-occupied Crimea is hit by Ukrainian drones and catches fire. ((RBC-Ukraine))
Ukrainian drones also hit Wildberries logistics hubs in Saint Petersburg and Tver, Russia. ((Kyiv Independent))

Ukrainian officials say a Russian ballistic missile strike on a private training ground hosting a defence-industry event in the Kyiv Oblast killed 10 people and injured nearly 100. Prosecutors investigate possible negligence in organizing the event. ((Reuters))
A Romanian F-16 ​fighter jet shot down a Russian Geran-2 drone near Padina, Buzău County, that had entered its airspace for the first ‌time. ((Euronews))
The North Kordofan government reports that 15 civilians in the Burbur area south of El-Obeid, Sudan have been killed by a Rapid Support Forces drone strike. ((Sudan Tribune))
At least 27 people are killed, including 12 militants, in an attack on a security check post in Tank District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. ((Hindustan Times))

The Gordie Howe International Bridge, which connects between Detroit, Michigan, U.S., and Windsor, Ontario, Canada, ceremonially opens, with Canadian officials marking the opening ceremony of the bridge with the absence of American officials amidst ongoing trade tensions. ((Detroit Free Press)) ((Reuters))
Paramount announces that they have agreed to delay its US$111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery amidst lawsuits from 12 U.S. state attorneys general. ((AFP via France 24)) ((The Hill))

French authorities evacuate more than 110,000 people from Cap Ferret, Gironde, by land and sea as an uncontrolled wildfire burns over 19,000 hectares, destroys 80 homes, and threatens the peninsula’s only access road. ((The Guardian))

Spanish interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska declares a national emergency over wildfires in the Community of Madrid and the Province of Ávila, placing the Military Emergencies Unit in command. Authorities evacuate more than 10,000 people as three major fires remain uncontrolled. ((AA))
Thirteen people are killed and two others are injured after a heavy boulder rolled down a hill and hit moving vehicles in Chamba District, India. ((Xinhua))
Five people are killed and three others are injured when a soil collapse buries a house in Hongtong County, Shanxi, China. ((Reuters))

Oxford University reports the first volunteer that has been injected with the Ebola vaccine aimed at targeting the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain of Ebola that is causing a outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. ((AFP via GMA News Online))

The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis, has spread to an additional four states: Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Pennsylvania. ((CNBC))
Michigan, U.S. surpasses 8,100 cases of cyclosporiasis. ((CBS News))
The U.S. CDC reports 2,318 confirmed measles cases in the country during the first seven months of 2026, marking the highest annual total since 1991. ((AFP via Euractiv))

The European Union sanctions five Iranian judges over alleged human rights violations and Ashiyane cyber group founder Nima Salehi, whom it accuses of cooperating with Iranian authorities to suppress information. ((Reuters))
The U.S. treasury department announces sanctions against nine firms and four people associated with sanctioned Iranian financer Babak Zanjani after attempting to evade previous sanctions. ((Reuters))

Venezuelan foreign minister Félix Plasencia says the country will withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC), citing alleged geographic bias. The ICC says it has not received formal notice and that existing investigations and cooperation obligations remain unaffected. ((AFP via RFI))

The U.S. state department, in coordination with the Mexican finance ministry, sanctions over 50 Mexican individuals and companies allegedly linked to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. ((Bloomberg)) ((El País))

A South African court temporarily halts the parliament's impeachment inquiry into president Cyril Ramaphosa over the theft of US$580,000 from his farm, pending his challenge to a report finding possible constitutional violations. ((Reuters))
Eight people are killed, including six children, in an arson and shooting attack at a house in Grand Haven Charter Township, Michigan, United States. ((ABC News)) ((The Indian Express))
Diplomatic sources say International Criminal Court member states voted to remove chief prosecutor Karim Ahmad Khan following sexual misconduct allegations. ((Al Jazeera)) ((CNN))

Prosecutors say thieves stole a 2,500-year-old gold Celtic necklace from the Musée du Pays Châtillonnais in Châtillon-sur-Seine, Côte-d'Or, France, after breaking its display case during opening hours. The artifact belongs to the Vix treasure. ((AFP via The Manila Times))
Bangladeshi president Mohammed Shahabuddin resigns from office, citing health reasons. ((Reuters))
Forty deputies of the Polish Sejm from the Law and Justice party resign as part of a dispute between party leader Jarosław Kaczyński and member Mateusz Morawiecki. ((AP)) ((Polsat ))
SpaceX Starship launched on test flight 13, being the first to to deploy operational Starlink satellites, then successfully soft landing in the Indian Ocean, intact without explosion.((CNN))
The United States strikes an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy naval academy in Ziba Kenar, Gilan province, Iran. ((Arab News)) ((Iran International))

Paramount announces that they have agreed to delay its US$111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery amidst lawsuits from twelve U.S. state attorneys general. ((AFP via France 24)) ((The Hill))
The death toll from the sinking of passenger ferry MV Barima off the coast of Guyana two days ago rises to 72. ((The Guardian))
The U.S. state of Michigan surpasses 8,100 cases of cyclosporiasis. ((CBS News))
The Sudan Doctors Union reports a dengue fever outbreak in Sudan's Blue Nile state, killing 39 people and leaving 300 infected. ((Sudan Tribune))
For the ninth consecutive day, thousands continue to protest in Kyiv, Ukraine, demanding Mykhailo Fedorov's reinstatement as Minister of Defence. ((The Kyiv Independent))
Forty deputies of the Polish Sejm leave the Law and Justice party as part of a dispute between party leader Jarosław Kaczyński and member Mateusz Morawiecki. ((AP)) ((Polsat ))

The White House Correspondents' Dinner is held at the Waldorf Astoria hotel in Washington, D.C., after being rescheduled following the assassination attempt at the Washington Hilton in April 2026. This is the first White House Correspondents' Dinner attended by U.S. President Donald Trump, after he previously skipped every dinner during his first term. ((Politico)) ((NPR))
The SpaceX Starship test flight 13, the first to successfully deploy operational Starlink satellites, successfully lands in the Indian Ocean intact. ((CNN))
